newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ shares falter at close, response to U.S. muted.
newsitem.headline: NZ shares falter at close, response to U.S. muted.

text.p: * NZ share market rally falters at close, ends slightly up
* Response muted to Wall Street's 2.64 pct rally
* FCL Paper, Forests end strongly
Price movements at close
LAST CHG * NZSE40 cap index +12.80 at 2,261.93
320 nil * NZSC cap index +13.86 at 4,938.91
320 +11 * NZMC .NZMC cap index +6.25 at 1,856.65
347 +6 * Volume NZ$62 million. Futures +7 at 1,130
647 +2 * Other movers - +4 +6
New Zealand share prices ended in positive territory on Wednesday but off their session high in a muted response to Wall Street's 2.64 percent rally.
The NZSE-40 Capital Index ended 12.80 points higher at 2,261.93, but off its peak of 2,249.13, on turnover worth a respectable NZ$62 million.

"The Dow is up 179 points, our interest rates have been down significantly in the last few days, so the market has got every reason to rally, but it's finding it difficult," Richard Burton at Cavill White Securities said.
"It's not a great response, but I guess the reason is the concerns about earnings," he said.

"And also it's only a one-day rise in the Dow. There is another (economic data) figure out tonight. It seems to go drunkenly from one figure to the next, so they don't tend to know which way it's going to go," he said.
U.S. stocks had rallied on a smaller-than-expected rise in wage inflation and the largest drop since August 1996 in manufactured-goods' orders. The market faces U.S. first quarter GDP tonight.
Fletcher Paper was sharply higher, up 11 cents at NZ$3.20, helped along by optimism that the pulp and paper outlook may be improving.
FCL Forests was also stronger, up four at NZ$1.99 but fellow forester Carter Holt Harvey was static at $3.20.
Summit Gold, which has come under pressure in recent days, regained six cents to NZ$0.36.
-- James Gray, Auckland newsroom +64 9 302 1253
